[quote=irocco;58793002][i]The message would rapidly be unencrypted and replied to swiftly, "Permission granted" Tower control replied with a voice hoarse from many days of work, barking orders at planes, he continued "Pull into runway 27, it's reserved for Diplomatic missions. There will be a car and a driver waiting for you there." just off to the side of the tarmac a sleek black car with a driver dressed in a fine suit awaited it's occupants.[/i] [/quote]
[i]The plane received the message and began its descent, coming into view of the crowds below. The old plane's cranky landing gears hissed sharply upon touchdown. As the pilot brought the plane to a stop, Hyong-yong chul and his guards prepared to exit the plane and begin their diplomatic mission, bags would be packed and seats checked to ensure that the plane was secure and that they'd be leaving with everything safely. Soon the hatch of the plane would let out a screech before the men would exit the plane. Immediately guards would swarm Hyong-yong chul and scan the outside area to see if it was devoid of potential threats. [/i]

[i]The small Iroccan crowd gathered at the window of the airport would watch as, for the first time in years, a new diplomatic plane would land on runway 27. Perhaps the aging Sealiph was not all poems and reconstruction, some thought. While others feared that this gigantic nation on a foreign continent sought to exploit the old age of their monarch. No matter their opinions, they were glad that the nation was at last reopening to diplomacy and trade, the same old Zabidiyan products they bought were high quality, they were happy to see that something new may hit their markets.

The driver would lazily step out of the vehicle, his eyes widening slightly as he saw the amount of guards surrounding what he assumed to be the diplomat, he called out to them "Sir! You will have to choose two guards to come with you. I do not have the capacity to bring... all of them." He said, sounding tired despite it still being early in the morning.[/i]

The small display screen began broadcasting the images from the rocket. The island became smaller and smaller as the rocket accelerated into the atmosphere. The rocket began to release its satellites into orbit. The sides of the rocket opened up and the satellites were boosted into space. The video feed from the satellite was now on the screen. The shamatine desert could be seen, and in the middle of it, a burning wreckage of a town. Oh no, muttered the president.
